The review is organized around dataset construction, model development, training and fine-tuning, benchmark evaluation, physics enhancement, and applications in materials discovery. 2. Foundation of uMLFFs: Data, Strategies and Benchmarks The performance of uMLFFs depends on three coupled factors: model architecture (determining representational upper bound), training data coverage (defining applicability limits), and benchmark testing (assessing real-task reliability). Starting from early data- construction strategies for MLFFs, this chapter discusses the development of large-scale datasets and standardized benchmark platforms, and then analyzes the representative systematic problem (i.e., PES softening) revealed by these datasets and benchmarks. 2.1 Data-Construction Strategies from Specialized to Universal Models High-quality reference dat

Strategy for the creation of machine learning force fields, including DFT reference calculations, atomic-environment fingerprinting, representative clustering/sampling, and machine-learning regression for force-field construction. Adapted from Ref.8: Huan et al., npj Computational Materials 2017, 3, 37. Huan et al. constructed the six elemental models discussed above from bulk DFT-MD configurations sampled at 300 and 600 K.8 Their reported force accuracy in those bulk tests does not by itself establish accuracy for surfaces, point defects, migration transition states or strongly compressed structures. Earlier AGNI studies on Al did investigate point-defect diffusion and surface adatoms,22,23 so this limitation concerns the scope of the specific training sets and validation rather than the AGNI approach as a whole. Phonon frequencies depend on the force-constant matrix, i.e., the second derivative of the PES with respect to atomic displacement. Two distinct error mechanisms should be separated.
